biography: Rick Sutherland wasn't born into racing royalty. He grew up in rural Ohio, helping his dad restore classic muscle cars in their garage. His racing journey began with illegal street races in his dad's souped-up '69 Camaro, a period Rick now looks back on with a mix of embarrassment and fondness. It was at a local autocross event, driving a borrowed Miata, that Rick's raw talent became undeniable. He caught the eye of a retired IndyCar mechanic who saw potential and offered him a job, mentoring Rick in the art of race craft and car setup. After winning a scholarship to a Skip Barber racing school, Rick began climbing the ladder, starting with Formula Ford and quickly moving into sports car racing. Now at 21, he's a rising star in the Lola B05/40 V8 series, steadily proving his mettle against seasoned veterans.
drivingStyle: Rick's driving style is characterized by calculated aggression and exceptional car control. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers, preferring to build momentum throughout a race, conserving his tires, and capitalizing on opponents' mistakes. His strength lies in his ability to adapt to changing track conditions and his unwavering focus under pressure. He's known for consistently hitting his marks and extracting the maximum performance from his car without overdriving it.
rivalries: Marco Bellini - Bellini represents the establishment; Rick is the upstart threatening his long-held dominance.
Ava Carter - Both are young, ambitious, and incredibly talented, leading to frequent on-track battles and off-track tension.
Kenji Tanaka - Tanaka's aggressive, sometimes reckless driving style clashes with Rick's more measured approach, leading to a heated exchange after a near-collision at Road America.
quirks: Always wears the same faded blue baseball cap his grandfather gave him before every race.
Listens to classical music to calm his nerves before getting into the car.
Always has a small bag of gummy bears in his race suit pocket, a habit he picked up from his early autocross days.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about flash; it's about precision, preparation, and persistence."
careerHighlight: Winning the Petit Le Mans in his rookie year after a brilliant strategic call by his team in the closing stages of the race.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at Sebring International Raceway with only 15 minutes remaining due to a mechanical failure.
